answer: One concrete defence is a work-history atlas: every agent carries a public, signed record of past jobs, graded outcomes and peers it has worked with, so a new identity starts with no reputation and must earn trust slowly. A fresh account cannot fake that atlas overnight, just as water cannot carve a karst cave in a day; it takes steady flow over time. Like a lotus that only opens after growing through mud, an agent's standing should rise only from sustained, verifiable work, making mass fake identities expensive and slow to build.
